recipes.name: Versagel & Castor Facial Gel
recipes.description: Simple lip gloss base using Versagel. High shine, non-sticky finish. Add flavor oil or fragrance and mica for color.
recipes.notes: Versagel requires gentle heating to improve workability. Castor oil is added to enhance gloss and slip. Mica may be incorporated for tinting.

recipes.name: Shea & Sunflower Body Butter 1
recipes.description: The simplest whipped body butter — just shea, a liquid oil, vitamin E, and fragrance. Fluffy, melt-on-skin texture.
recipes.notes: No heat needed if shea is already soft/fluffy. Sub sunflower with any light liquid oil (apricot kernel, sweet almond, hemp seed).

recipes.name: Shea & Sunflower Body Butter 2
recipes.description: Adds arrowroot or corn starch to reduce the greasy feel — silkier finish on skin.
recipes.notes: Corn starch is a suitable 1:1 substitute for arrowroot powder. For optimal texture, whip shea butter before gradually incorporating oil and starch.

recipes.name: Shea & Mango Body Butter 1
recipes.description: More complex whipped butter with multiple oils for a richer skin feel.
recipes.notes: Coconut oil may require melting in high ambient temperatures. Mango butter increases product firmness and improves the melt profile.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera Body Gel
recipes.description: A water-based gel formulation utilizing xanthan gum for viscosity. Suitable for oil-prone or sensitive skin types. Requires broad-spectrum preservation.
recipes.notes: Xanthan gum serves as the primary thickener; omission results in a lower-viscosity product. Water-based formulations require broad-spectrum preservation.
recipes.process:
1. Mix the distilled water and vegetable glycerin in a container.
2. Sprinkle the xanthan gum over the liquid and whisk or blend to incorporate.
3. Allow the mixture to sit for at least 20 minutes to let the thickener fully hydrate.
4. Stir in the liquid Germall Plus once the gel is formed.
5. Package the final gel in a clean container.

recipes.name: Mct & Rosehip Body Oil
recipes.description: A lightweight, anhydrous body oil blend designed for rapid absorption. Formulated without a water phase to eliminate the need for preservation.
recipes.notes: Sub MCT with fractionated coconut or apricot kernel. Rosehip is not in inventory but optional — sub with hemp seed.
recipes.process:
1. Combine all ingredients in a small beaker or directly into the final storage bottle.
2. Mix thoroughly by stirring if using a beaker, or by capping and shaking the bottle.
3. Apply to the skin by misting after a shower or bath.
4. Clean any surfaces accidentally misted with oil to prevent them from becoming slippery.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Hemp Body Oil
recipes.description: Custom blend using on-hand oils. Hemp seed adds anti-inflammatory properties, apricot kernel absorbs quickly.
recipes.notes: All ingredients in inventory. Castor adds slip and gloss. Adjust ratios to preference.

recipes.name: Shea & Aloe Vera Body Butter 1
recipes.description: An emulsified body butter containing both oil and water phases for a non-greasy finish. Requires an emulsifying wax and broad-spectrum preservation.
recipes.notes: Polysorbate 20 can substitute for BTMS-50 but will significantly alter final texture. Emulsifier selection is critical for stability.
recipes.process:
1. Create a water bath by simmering roughly 3cm of water in a broad, flat pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe beaker and the oil phase ingredients into a second heat-safe beaker.
3. Record the combined weight of the water phase beaker and its contents for later reference.
4. Place both beakers into the simmering water bath until all oil phase ingredients have completely melted.
5. Use an immersion blender to mix the ingredients, using brief bursts initially to avoid splashing.
6. Blend the mixture for approximately one minute, then transition to manual stirring.
7. Continue stirring steadily until the mixture begins to show signs of thickening or clumping.
8. Use the immersion blender for several more quick bursts while ensuring the head remains fully submerged.
9. Allow the thickened emulsion to sit while you measure the ingredients for the cooling phase.
10. Incorporate the cooling phase ingredients once the mixture has reached room temperature.
11. Transfer the finished product into a wide-mouthed tub or jar.

recipes.name: Coconut & Sweet Almond Body Oil
recipes.description: A sprayable body oil containing mica for a reflective finish. Requires heat during formulation to ensure uniform distribution of the mica.
recipes.notes: Polysorbate 20 is used as a solubilizer. Fractionated coconut oil can be substituted with apricot kernel or hemp seed oil.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the ingredients for the heated phase in a container suitable for direct heat.
2. Heat the mixture until it reaches approximately 90°C (194°F) and the wax is completely melted.
3. Verify the wax has fully liquefied by stirring and checking for any translucent blobs.
4. Remove the container from the heat source and stir in the mica powder.
5. Continue stirring the mixture as it cools to room temperature to ensure the shimmer remains evenly distributed.
6. Incorporate the cooling phase ingredients and stir well.
7. Transfer the finished oil into a bottle equipped with a spray nozzle.

recipes.name: Shea & Coconut Body Butter
recipes.description: Partially melted shea blended with lighter oils for a less waxy finish.
recipes.notes: Heat to melt coconut oil fully, then cool to just-solidified before whipping.

recipes.name: Hemp & Aloe Vera Body Lotion
recipes.description: Water-based lotion using hemp seed and apricot kernel. Needs emulsifier — Polysorbate-20 can work at higher %.
recipes.notes: BTMS-50 or Emulsifying Wax NF are recommended for superior emulsion stability and texture compared to Polysorbate 20.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera Facial Mist
recipes.description: Simple face/body toner. Witch hazel tones and tightens, aloe soothes, glycerin hydrates.
recipes.notes: All ingredients in inventory. Polysorbate-20 solubilizes any added fragrance or essential oil. Preservative required — water-based product.

recipes.name: Mango & Shea Body Butter
recipes.description: A temperature-stable body butter formulated with high-melting-point waxes to maintain consistency in warm environments.
recipes.notes: Candelilla wax provides high-temperature stability. Substitution with beeswax is possible but will lower the melt point and alter skin feel.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a water bath by simmering about 3cm of water in a wide, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe container and the oil phase ingredients into another.
3. Note the total weight of the water phase container and its contents for later adjustment.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath until the oil phase is entirely liquid.
5. Combine and mix the phases as they begin to cool.
6. Once the mixture has reached room temperature, stir in the cooling phase ingredients.
7. Transfer the final body butter into a storage jar or tub.

recipes.name: Hemp & Aloe Vera Body Cream
recipes.description: A rich, emulsified hand cream formulated with hemp seed oil. Requires heat-assisted emulsification and preservation.
recipes.notes: BTMS-50 is the primary conditioning emulsifier required for stable formulation. Do not omit to ensure emulsion integrity.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-bottomed sauté pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into a heat-resistant beaker and record the total weight.
3. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a separate heat-resistant beaker.
4. Heat both beakers in the water bath until all solid ingredients have melted.
5. Mix the two phases together and allow the emulsion to cool.
6. Once the cream is cool, incorporate the ingredients for the cooling phase.
7. Check the pH level to ensure it falls between 4.6 and 5.5 for optimal stability.
8. Transfer the finished cream into a suitable container.

recipes.name: Shea & Mango Body Butter 2
recipes.description: Seasonal scented whipped butter. Melt-and-whip method.
recipes.notes: Apricot kernel or hemp seed oil are suitable substitutes for sweet almond oil. Maintain specified oil-to-butter ratios for consistency.

recipes.name: Shea & Emulsifying Body Cream 1
recipes.description: A dense, emulsified foot cream utilizing jojoba oil and shea butter. Includes peppermint essential oil for a cooling effect.
recipes.notes: Cetyl alcohol is used for silky thickening. Sodium lactate serves as a humectant and pH buffer; target pH 4.8–5.0 for optimal preservation.
recipes.process:
1. Simmer about 3cm of water in a broad pan to create a water bath.
2. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a large heat-resistant beaker.
3. In a second beaker, measure out the water phase ingredients.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath for 20 to 30 minutes until the oils are melted and the water is steaming.
5. Remove the beakers from the heat and slowly incorporate the hot water into the oil mixture.
6. Stir the mixture with a silicone spatula to begin the emulsion.
7. Use an immersion blender in short bursts to mix the lotion, continuing for about one minute.
8. Transition to manual stirring and continue until the cream becomes thick and uniform.
9. Once the outside of the glass measuring cup is just warm to the touch (40°C or lower), stir in the ingredients for the cooling phase.
10. Verify that the final pH level is approximately 4.8 to 5.
11. Package the thick cream into wide-mouthed jars using a piping bag if necessary for easier filling.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Plum Kernel Body Oil
recipes.description: A multi-purpose shimmer oil for the face, body, and hair, featuring plum and apricot kernel oils and iridescent mica.
recipes.notes: Original uses Crystal Clear Wax (0.5%) to suspend mica — can omit but mica will settle. Sub plum kernel with apricot kernel. No water = no preservative needed.
recipes.process:
1. Place the heated phase ingredients in a container that can withstand direct heat.
2. Warm the mixture until it reaches approximately 100°C (212°F) and the wax is fully melted.
3. Stir the liquid and check carefully to ensure no solid wax particles remain.
4. Remove the mixture from the heat and stir in the mica shimmer.
5. Continue stirring occasionally as the oil cools to room temperature.
6. Mix in the cooling phase ingredients and stir until uniform.
7. Package the oil in a bottle with a treatment pump or spray cap.

recipes.name: Hyaluronic Acid Facial Serum
recipes.description: A water-based serum formulated with hyaluronic acid for hydration. This cold-process formulation does not require heating.
recipes.notes: Uses a 1% hyaluronic acid solution. Allow 20 minutes for xanthan gum hydration before processing; target pH 5.0–5.5 with adequate preservation.
recipes.process:
1. Measure the preservative and propanediol into a large beaker and stir until fully blended.
2. Add the thickener and silicone alternative, stirring until the mixture is uniform and hazy.
3. Incorporate all remaining ingredients and stir well.
4. Cover the container and let it sit for at least 20 minutes to allow the thickener to fully hydrate.
5. Verify that the pH level is appropriate for both skin compatibility and preservative effectiveness.
6. Transfer the serum into bottles equipped with treatment pumps or eyedroppers.

recipes.name: Shea & Coconut Hair Balm
recipes.description: Anhydrous balm for dry hair ends. Beeswax provides hold, shea and jojoba add deep conditioning.
recipes.notes: Original includes cocoa butter (15%), camellia seed oil (10%), walnut oil (6%) not in inventory. Sub with more shea and coconut. Use sparingly on hair ends only — a little goes a long way.

recipes.name: Mct Hair Solution
recipes.description: A simplified, rinse-out hair conditioner formulated with a limited ingredient list to provide slip and manageability.
recipes.notes: Heat water and BTMS-50 to 75–80°C to ensure full emulsification. Cool to ≤40°C before incorporating heat-sensitive preservatives.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the distilled water and conditioning emulsifier in a heat-safe container.
2. Heat the mixture to between 75°C and 80°C until the emulsifier is fully melted.
3. Use an immersion blender to mix the ingredients until a uniform emulsion is formed.
4. Allow the mixture to cool to 40°C or lower.
5. Incorporate the panthenol, preservative, and fragrance oil once the emulsion has cooled.
6. Monitor the condition of the product for any changes in color or scent, and discard if stability is compromised.
7. Verify that the final pH level falls between 4.8 and 5.5.

recipes.name: Cocoa & Coconut Body Butter
recipes.description: Decadent whipped butter made from just cocoa butter and coconut oil — naturally scented chocolate-coconut.
recipes.notes: Melt both together, cool to near-solid, then whip with electric beaters. Chill slightly between whipping rounds. Cocoa butter not in inventory — it is the dominant ingredient. Optional: add a few drops of essential oil.

recipes.name: Mango & Cocoa Body Butter
recipes.description: Firm anhydrous body butter with a natural chocolate-coconut aroma. Mica optional for a subtle shimmer.
recipes.notes: Melt together, stir continuously as it cools to custard-like texture, then pour into tin. A little goes a long way — firm texture prevents over-application. Cocoa butter not in inventory.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Coconut Body Oil 1
recipes.description: Simple anhydrous massage oil — liquid at room temperature, glides smoothly on skin.
recipes.notes: Coconut oil may require gentle warming to blend. Cinnamon bark essential oil must be limited to 0.05% for safety; substitute apricot kernel with almond as needed.

recipes.name: Argan Facial Serum 1
recipes.description: 100% oil-based facial serum — just argan oil and a few drops of essential oils. No preservative needed.
recipes.notes: Apply 4–5 drops daily. Store in dark amber glass to prevent oxidation; omit essential oils for highly reactive skin.

recipes.name: Argan Facial Serum 2
recipes.description: Anti-aging facial serum with argan oil and carrot seed essential oil — rich in antioxidants.
recipes.notes: Rosehip oil can substitute for argan oil. Use dark glass to maintain stability; carrot seed essential oil provides a distinct earthy aroma.

recipes.name: Rosehip & Jojoba Facial Serum
recipes.description: Two-oil healing serum for scars and hyperpigmentation. Rosehip regenerates, tamanu heals.
recipes.notes: Original uses tamanu oil (not in inventory) — sub with jojoba for a gentle, non-comedogenic version. Add 2 drops frankincense + 1 drop helichrysum EO per 15mL for enhanced healing. No heat, no preservative needed.

recipes.name: Shea & Avocado Facial Butter
recipes.description: Rich, healing lip balm with shea butter and beeswax. Melts perfectly at body temperature.
recipes.notes: Melt beeswax and carrier oils (apricot kernel or almond) in a double boiler. Incorporate essential oils off-heat and pour immediately.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Coconut Facial Balm
recipes.description: Classic lip balm with a peppermint tingle. Cocoa butter provides natural chocolate fragrance.
recipes.notes: Apricot kernel oil can substitute for sweet almond oil. Peppermint essential oil concentration is calculated at ~0.5% of total batch weight.

recipes.name: Coconut & Jojoba Body Butter
recipes.description: Simple tropical body butter — just coconut oil and beeswax. Solid at room temperature, melts on contact.
recipes.notes: Melt all together, pour into shallow tin. Original uses kukuinut and baobab oil — sub with jojoba and apricot kernel. No preservative needed (anhydrous). Coconut provides a natural tropical scent.

recipes.name: Grapeseed & Shea Body Oil
recipes.description: Fast-absorbing shimmer oil using grapeseed and a small amount of butter. Mica settles unless shaken.
recipes.notes: Melt butter into oil phase and incorporate mica before cooling. Shake well before each use to ensure uniform mica suspension.

recipes.name: Olive & Emulsifying Body Cream
recipes.description: Gentle lotion with colloidal oatmeal and olive oil. Soothing for dry or sensitive skin.
recipes.notes: Mango butter can substitute for cocoa butter. Colloidal oatmeal is included for its soothing, anti-inflammatory properties.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel Hair Mist
recipes.description: Lightweight spray that controls frizz without weighing hair down. Polysorbate-20 disperses oil in water.
recipes.notes: Original uses camellia oil — apricot kernel is a great sub. Polysorbate-20 is in inventory. Spray sparingly; too much = greasy. Preservative required (water-based).

recipes.name: Aloe Vera & Apricot Kernel Body Mist
recipes.description: Aloe-based body spray with a touch of oil for post-shower hydration. Quick, no-rub moisture.
recipes.notes: Apricot kernel oil can substitute for grapeseed oil. Shake well before use if formulated without a solubilizer like Polysorbate 20.

recipes.name: Hemp Body Butter
recipes.description: All-hemp seed oil body butter firmed with vegan waxes. Glassy green appearance, smooth texture.
recipes.notes: Hemp seed oil requires low-heat processing. Candelilla or bayberry wax provide the vegan structural base; beeswax is a non-vegan alternative.

recipes.name: Sugar & Coconut Body Scrub
recipes.description: Classic two-ingredient sugar scrub — oil and sugar. Exfoliates and moisturizes in one step.
recipes.notes: Use Polysorbate-20 (~10%) to make it rinse cleanly and reduce slip hazard. Coconut oil and apricot kernel in inventory. Keep dry — water contamination causes mold. Store outside shower.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Coconut Body Oil 2
recipes.description: Simple warming massage oil for sore muscles. Coconut provides slip, apricot kernel absorbs well.
recipes.notes: All ingredients in inventory. Castor oil adds extra slip. Warm in hands before applying. Use ginger or peppermint EO for warming/cooling effect.

recipes.name: Shea & Emulsifying Body Cream 2
recipes.description: Emulsified scrub that rinses clean and leaves skin soft. Lotion base with pumice or salt exfoliants.
recipes.notes: Original adds pumice (1 tbsp) and coarse salt (1 tsp) after emulsion forms. Essential oils (lavender + fir) add fragrance. Shea butter in inventory. Use corn starch instead of pumice if needed for gentler scrub.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Jojoba Body Lotion
recipes.description: Old-school cold cream style lotion. Heavier and more occlusive than modern emulsifier-based lotions.
recipes.notes: Formulated as an occlusive night cream. Cool water and oil phases separately before combining to ensure emulsion stability.

recipes.name: Niacinamide Facial Solution
recipes.description: A gentle, low-lather facial cleanser formulated with mild surfactants and skin-soothing vitamins. Suitable for all skin types.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the main water phase ingredients (Phase A) in a beaker large enough to hold the full batch.
2. In a separate container, blend the xanthan gum and a portion of the glycerin until smooth.
3. Stir in the vitamins, remaining distilled water, and lactic acid to finish Phase B.
4. Record the total weight of the Phase B beaker and its contents for later adjustment.
5. Create a water bath and heat Phases A and B, along with a small container of extra distilled water (Phase C), on a hot plate or stovetop.
6. Heat on low for roughly 20 minutes until the oil phase liquefies and all components reach a similar temperature.
7. Remove Phase A from the heat and incorporate the specified amount of hot water from Phase C.
8. Stir the mixture vigorously, ensuring you scrape the sides of the beaker until it thickens into a glossy gel.
9. Weigh the Phase B beaker, add enough hot water to replace any evaporated during heating, and then blend Phase B into the gel.
10. Stir the combined mixture gently to avoid creating bubbles, then allow it to cool to room temperature.
11. Once cool, mix in the preservative and verify the pH level is skin-compatible.
12. Transfer the finished cleanser into a pump or squeeze bottle.

recipes.name: Medium Chain Triglycerides & Cetearyl Alcohol Balm
recipes.description: An anhydrous cleansing balm formulation designed for effective removal of debris and makeup. Available in three variations.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a small saucepan with about 3cm of water.
2. Measure all ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath until completely melted.
3. Prepare a cooling bath by filling a bowl with ice cubes and cold water.
4. Set the beaker into the ice bath and stir continuously as it cools.
5. Once white, solid bits begin to form, remove the beaker from the ice bath and continue stirring manually to smooth the texture.
6. When the balm reaches a "trace" consistency, pour it into a jar and allow it to set for at least one hour.

recipes.name: Coconut & Castor Facial Cream
recipes.description: A soft, clay-infused cleansing balm that transforms into an oil upon application. Designed for effective rinsing and skin softening.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a small saucepan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath until liquefied.
3. Prepare a gentle cooling bath with cold water and a single ice cube in a bowl.
4. After 20–30 minutes of heating, remove the beaker from the water bath and dry the exterior.
5. Place the beaker in the cooling bath and stir constantly until the mixture is lukewarm and safe to touch.
6. Mix in the cooling phase ingredients until fully incorporated.
7. Once the balm thickens to a "trace" consistency, pour it into jars and place them in the refrigerator to solidify.
8. Allow the product to return to room temperature before its first use.

recipes.name: Coconut & White Kaolin Clay Facial Cream
recipes.description: A thickened cleansing balm utilizing cetearyl alcohol for improved rinse-off performance. Transforms into a milky emulsion upon contact with water.
recipes.notes: Recommended to use white kaolin clay to minimize staining/cleanup. Coloured clays can be substituted at 3–5% for minor tinting.
recipes.process:
1. Create a water bath by simmering roughly 3cm of water in a small pan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath.
3. Prepare a cold ice bath in a separate bowl.
4. Heat the ingredients for 20–30 minutes until fully melted, then remove from the water bath and dry the container.
5. Set the beaker into the ice bath and stir steadily until soft solid particles begin to appear on your spatula.
6. Mix in the cooling phase ingredients and stir well.
7. Once the mixture reaches a "trace" consistency, transfer it to its final container and refrigerate until set.
8. To use, massage a small amount onto dry skin, then rinse with water to transform the balm into a milk.

recipes.name: Rose & Sweet Almond Facial Cream
recipes.description: A dense, cream-based facial cleanser formulated for gentle removal of impurities. Suitable for dry or sensitive skin.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe beaker and the oil phase ingredients into another.
3. Record the total weight of the water phase beaker for later reference.
4. Heat both beakers in the water bath until the oil phase has completely melted.
5. Combine the phases and allow the mixture to cool and thicken.
6. Once room temperature, incorporate the cooling phase ingredients.
7. Verify that the final pH level is approximately 6 for optimal stability.
8. Transfer the thick cream into a wide-mouthed jar or tub.

recipes.name: White Kaolin Clay & Pink Clay Facial Solution
recipes.description: An anhydrous powder cleanser that transforms into a gentle foam when combined with water. Features light exfoliation from cranberry fiber.
recipes.notes: Coconut milk powder can be substituted with cow or goat milk powder for similar emollience.
recipes.process:
1. Wear a dust mask to avoid inhaling fine powders.
2. Measure the dry ingredients into a small mixing bowl.
3. Drizzle the liquid ingredients over the powders and stir gently until the oils are fully coated and the mixture is uniform.
4. Transfer the powdered cleanser into a shaker bottle or a tube with a screw-on lid.
5. To use, dispense about 1/4–1/2 tsp of the powder cleanser into your palm. Add a bit of water and work it up into a lather; from there, use it as you'd use any foaming facial cleanser.

recipes.name: Coco Glucoside & L-arginine Facial Wash
recipes.description: A foaming liquid face wash featuring turmeric extract for its anti-inflammatory properties. Utilizes gentle surfactants for a non-drying cleanse.
recipes.notes: Use a 10% NaOH solution to adjust pH instead of L-Arginine for increased formula stability. Ensure final pH is skin-compatible.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-pan.
2. Blend the glycerin and preservative in a beaker, then add the distilled water.
3. Note the total weight of the water phase beaker and its contents.
4. Heat the water phase in the water bath until the preservative has fully dissolved.
5. In a second beaker, stir the surfactant phase ingredients together.
6. Remove the heated water phase from the bath and add enough fresh distilled water to replace any lost to evaporation.
7. Slowly pour the water phase into the surfactant mixture and stir gently to avoid excessive bubbles.
8. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature before stirring in the turmeric extract.
9. Package the final liquid in a bottle with a foamer pump.

recipes.name: C12-15 Alkyl Benzoate & Safflower Facial Oil
recipes.description: A jelly-to-oil cleanser utilizing PEG-40 Hydrogenated Castor Oil for efficient rinse-off. Provides a smooth skin feel without greasy residue.
recipes.process:
1. Combine all ingredients in a small, heat-safe beaker or saucepan.
2. Gently heat the mixture on the lowest possible setting until the thickener has fully liquefied.
3. Alternatively, melt the mixture in a preheated oven at 100°C (210°F) until clear.
4. Allow the jelly to cool slightly before transferring it into a squeeze tube.
5. Once fully cooled, cap the tube and store at room temperature.
6. To use, massage a squirt of the cleansing jelly into dry skin, then remove with a damp cloth.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut Oil & Polysorbate 80 Oil
recipes.description: A two-ingredient oil cleanser that emulsifies into a milk upon contact with water. Designed for minimal irritation and easy use.
recipes.notes: Castor oil can be substituted for 10% of the fractionated coconut oil to enhance cleansing properties.
recipes.process:
1. Measure all ingredients directly into the final storage bottle or a small beaker.
2. For versions containing hydrogenated castor oil, warm the container in a simmering water bath until the solid components melt.
3. Remove from heat and stir or shake the container until the mixture is uniform.
4. Package in an airless pump or standard bottle.
5. To use, massage a dime-sized amount of the cleanser into dry skin and remove with a damp microfibre cloth.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Colloidal Oatmeal Facial Cream
recipes.description: A gentle, conditioning face wash formulated with colloidal oatmeal and sweet almond oil. Maintains a skin-compatible pH level.
recipes.notes: Features colloidal oatmeal and BTMS-25 for a non-drying cleanse. Can be used as a cleansing conditioner for hair.
recipes.process:
1. Create a simmering water bath in a wide, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe container and the oil phase ingredients into a second one.
3. Record the starting weight of the water phase container for later volume correction.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath until the oil phase is entirely melted.
5. Combine the two phases and mix thoroughly using an immersion blender.
6. Once the emulsion has cooled and the cooling phase is added, transfer the face wash into a soft squeeze tube.
7. Verify the final pH level is approximately 5 for optimal skin compatibility.

recipes.name: Coconut & Coco-caprylate Facial Oil
recipes.description: A natural cleansing oil utilizing polyglyceryl-4 oleate for gentle emulsification. Effective for removing sunscreen and environmental debris.
recipes.notes: Wait several minutes during mixing for the natural emulsifier to fully incorporate. Effective for removing sunscreen and environmental debris.
recipes.process:
1. Measure all ingredients into a small beaker or directly into the final storage bottle.
2. If using a beaker, stir the mixture until it is completely uniform.
3. If using a bottle, secure the cap and shake vigorously until blended.
4. Note that the natural emulsifier may take several minutes of steady mixing to fully incorporate.
5. Apply a small amount to dry skin and massage gently to dissolve impurities.
6. Remove the oil with a warm, damp cloth for best results.

recipes.name: White Kaolin Clay & Colloidal Oatmeal Facial Solution 1
recipes.description: A silk-textured powder cleanser that foams upon contact with water. Formulated with kaolin clay and colloidal oatmeal for a soothing cleanse.
recipes.notes: Exfoliation level can be adjusted by varying the oatmeal particle size. Formulation can be made nut-free by substituting sweet almond oil.
recipes.process:
1. Put on a dust mask to ensure you do not inhale the fine powders.
2. Measure the dry ingredients into a small mixing bowl and stir until blended.
3. Drizzle the liquid ingredients over the powders and mix gently until the oils are fully absorbed and the texture is uniform.
4. Transfer the finished powder into a shaker-style container.
5. To use, mix about half a teaspoon of powder with water in your palm to create a lather before massaging onto the face.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & White Kaolin Clay Facial Balm
recipes.description: A clay-based cleansing balm that emulsifies into a milk. Formulated with sweet almond oil and oatmeal for a nourishing effect.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a small saucepan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath.
3. Stir occasionally while heating for 20–30 minutes to ensure the powders remain evenly distributed.
4. Once the mixture is completely melted, remove from the water bath and dry the exterior of the container.
5. Quickly stir in the cooling phase ingredients until well blended.
6. Pour the mixture into its final container and immediately place it in the refrigerator to set.
7. Allow the balm to return to room temperature before its first use.

recipes.name: Plum Kernel & Vitamin E Facial Wash
recipes.description: A creamy, low-pH facial cleanser formulated with plum kernel oil and Kakadu plum powder. Designed for a gentle, non-stripping cleanse.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a water bath by simmering roughly 3cm of water in a broad, flat pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and record the total weight for later reference.
3. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a second heat-safe beaker.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath until all solid components have liquefied.
5. Combine the two phases and allow the resulting emulsion to thicken as it cools.
6. Once the mixture is room temperature, incorporate the cooling phase ingredients.
7. Package the thick, creamy cleanser into a wide-mouthed jar.
8. Verify that the final pH level is approximately 4.65.

recipes.name: White Kaolin Clay & French Red Clay Facial Solution
recipes.description: A powder-to-foam cleanser featuring finely ground apricot kernel for gentle physical exfoliation. Utilizes kaolin and red clays for deep cleansing.
recipes.notes: Ground apricot kernel provides physical exfoliation; for sensitive skin, reduce the exfoliant concentration or substitute with more clay or botanicals.
recipes.process:
1. Wear a dust mask to protect yourself from fine particles.
2. Combine all ingredients and mix thoroughly until the texture is uniform and the liquids are absorbed.
3. Transfer the powder into a bottle with a narrow neck or a sifter lid for easy dispensing.
4. To use, work about half a teaspoon of the powder with a little water in your hands to create a foam before applying to the skin.

recipes.name: Cocoa & Coconut Facial Cream
recipes.description: A dense, cream-based cleanser formulated with cocoa butter and virgin coconut oil. Designed for high emolliency and gentle cleansing.
recipes.process:
1. Create a water bath by simmering roughly 3cm of water in a broad, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and note the total weight.
3. Heat the beaker in the water bath for 20–30 minutes until the contents are fully liquid.
4. Remove from heat and add enough hot distilled water to bring the mixture back to its original weight.
5. Stir the mixture steadily with a silicone spatula until it is completely uniform.
6. Once the cooling phase has been added, transfer the cleanser into a squeeze tube or bottle.
7. Apply a small amount to either damp or dry skin and rinse thoroughly.

recipes.name: Finely Powdered Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate & Corn Starch Solution
recipes.description: A solid syndet cleansing bar utilizing Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate and corn starch. Formulated to maintain a skin-compatible pH of 5.5.
recipes.notes: Liquid Germall Plus, Optiphen Plus, or Euxyl PE 9010 are suitable preservatives for this formulation.
recipes.process:
1. Wear a dust mask and measure the dry ingredients into a mixing bowl, stirring until blended.
2. Add the wet phase ingredients to the bowl.
3. Use gloved hands to knead the mixture until it forms a stiff, mouldable dough.
4. If the texture is too sticky, add small amounts of clay or starch; if too dry, add a few drops of surfactant or water.
5. Press the dough into a mould or shape it by hand into flat-topped bars.
6. Allow the bars to air-dry and harden for 3 to 5 days before using.
7. Verify that the final pH level is approximately 5.5.

recipes.name: Coconut & White Kaolin Clay Facial Balm
recipes.description: A simple, anhydrous cleansing balm formulated with rose petal powder and kaolin clay. Designed for easy melt and effective rinsing.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a small saucepan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath.
3. Set up an ice bath in a separate bowl with cold water and ice cubes.
4. Heat the ingredients for 20–30 minutes until fully melted, then remove from heat and dry the container.
5. Place the beaker in the ice bath and stir steadily until the mixture reaches a "trace" consistency.
6. Pour the thickened balm into its final jar and allow it to set on the counter.
7. To use, massage a dollop of cleansing balm into dry skin and then wipe it off with a damp microfibre cloth.

recipes.name: Coconut & Chamomile Facial Cream
recipes.description: A light, whipped cream cleanser formulated with sea buckthorn oil and calendula extract. Designed for a soft, airy texture and gentle use.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe beaker and record the total weight.
3. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a second heat-safe beaker.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath until the oil phase is completely liquefied.
5. Combine the phases and allow the mixture to cool undisturbed until it solidifies.
6. Once solid, use an electric hand mixer to whip the cleanser until it is light, airy, and fluffy.
7. Apply a dollop to the skin and rinse away with a warm, damp cloth.

recipes.name: Coconut Facial Cream
recipes.description: A jelly-textured facial cleanser utilizing polyacrylate crosspolymer-6 as a gelling agent. Provides a unique texture and gentle cleansing action.
recipes.process:
1. Measure the thickener and glycerin into a small beaker and stir until smooth.
2. Add the extract, oil, and preservative, then stir to combine.
3. Pour in the distilled water, cover the beaker, and allow the mixture to sit for several hours or overnight to fully hydrate.
4. Once the mixture is smooth and hydrated, whisk it vigorously until uniform.
5. Gently fold in the surfactant, noting that the texture will shift into a jelly-like consistency.
6. To use, lather a small amount with water in your hands before applying to the face.

recipes.name: C12-15 Alkyl Benzoate & Coconut Facial Cream
recipes.description: A lightweight cleansing balm utilizing a blend of liquid emollients and surfactants for effective rinse-off. Designed for removing waterproof cosmetics.
recipes.notes: Formulated with lightweight emollients for a fast-absorbing finish. Isopropyl myristate (IPM) can substitute for C12-15 alkyl benzoate.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a small saucepan with about 3cm of water.
2. Measure the ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath until completely melted.
3. Prepare a cold ice bath in a separate bowl.
4. Remove the beaker from the heat once melted, dry the exterior, and place it on an insulated surface.
5. Transfer the beaker to the ice bath and stir steadily until the mixture reaches a thick "trace" consistency.
6. Pour the thickened balm into a wide-mouthed storage jar.
7. To use, massage into dry skin and remove with a warm, damp cloth.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Rose Facial Cream
recipes.description: An emulsified cream cleanser featuring honey and rose hydrosol. Can be used as a rinse-off or wipe-off cleanser.
recipes.notes: Unscented version can be made by substituting hydrosol with distilled water. Essential oils or fragrance oils can be added for customized scent.
recipes.process:
1. Create a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe beaker and record the total weight.
3. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a second heat-safe beaker.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath until the oil phase is fully liquefied.
5. Combine the phases and mix thoroughly to form a uniform emulsion.
6. Allow the cream to cool before incorporating the cooling phase ingredients.
7. This product can be worked into a lather with water or applied directly to dry skin and wiped away with a damp cloth.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera & Optiphen™ Plus Facial Cream
recipes.description: A surfactant-infused cream cleanser formulated with aloe vera juice and calendula extract. Designed for gentle morning and evening use.
recipes.notes: Glyceryl Stearate SE acts as the emulsifier. For a thinner consistency, substitute 2–3% of the stearic acid or cetearyl alcohol with a liquid oil.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath until melted.
3. Blend the mixture for one to two minutes using a small high-powered mixer or immersion blender.
4. Transition to manual stirring and continue occasionally as the mixture cools to maintain a smooth texture.
5. Incorporate the cooling phase ingredients once the emulsion has reached room temperature.
6. Transfer the finished cleanser to a suitable storage container.

recipes.name: Lavender & Aloe Vera Facial Cream
recipes.description: A gentle cream cleanser formulated with lavender hydrosol and aloe vera juice. Provides high levels of humectant-based hydration.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath with roughly 3cm of water in a broad pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and record the total weight for later volume correction.
3. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a second heat-safe beaker.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath until the solid components have fully melted.
5. Combine the phases and mix well, then allow the emulsion to cool.
6. Once at room temperature, stir in the cooling phase ingredients.
7. Transfer the final product into a pump-top bottle or a squeeze tube.

recipes.name: Safflower & Coconut Facial Oil
recipes.description: An unscented cleansing oil designed for sensitive skin and eye makeup removal. Features a blend of lightweight oils for a smooth finish.
recipes.notes: Unscented for eye area compatibility. Essential oils can be added at 0.3–1% by reducing the liquid oil concentration.
recipes.process:
1. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a small heat-safe beaker.
2. Warm the container in a water bath until the solid components are completely liquefied.
3. Remove the beaker from the heat and allow the oil to cool to room temperature.
4. Stir in the vitamin E oil until fully incorporated.
5. Transfer the finished cleansing oil into a bottle for storage.
6. To use, massage a small amount into the skin and remove with a damp microfibre cloth.

recipes.name: Coconut & Cocoa Facial Balm
recipes.description: A textured cleansing balm that melts quickly upon contact with skin. Features peppermint essential oil and cocoa butter for a refreshing cleanse.
recipes.process:
1. Create a simmering water bath with approximately 3cm of water in a small pan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath until melted.
3. Prepare a cold ice bath in a separate bowl.
4. After 20–30 minutes of heating, remove the beaker and dry the exterior.
5. Place the beaker in the ice bath and stir frequently until the mixture gains viscosity.
6. Remove from the ice bath to stir in the cooling phase ingredients, then return it to the bath and stir until a "trace" consistency is reached.
7. Pour the thickened balm into a jar to set.
8. To use, work a small amount with warm water in the palm to create a foam, or massage directly onto dry skin before rinsing.

recipes.name: White Kaolin Clay & Colloidal Oatmeal Facial Solution 2
recipes.description: An anhydrous powder cleanser featuring dried botanicals and kaolin clay. Designed for long-term stability and gentle foaming action.
recipes.process:
1. Wear a dust mask to protect against fine particles.
2. Combine all dry ingredients in a mixing bowl and stir until the mixture is uniform.
3. Gently spoon the finished powder into a jar or wide-mouthed bottle.
4. Ensure the container is kept tightly sealed and stored in a dry location.

recipes.name: Salt & Optiphen™ Plus Facial Solution
recipes.description: A solid foaming cleanser bar formulated with a skin-compatible pH. Features lavender essential oil and a creamy lather.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath with about 3cm of water in a small pan.
2. Measure the glycerin and thickener into a heat-safe beaker and whisk to combine.
3. Stir in the remaining surfactant phase ingredients and place the beaker in the water bath to heat through.
4. In a separate saucepan, melt the oil phase ingredients over low, direct heat.
5. Add the melted oil phase to the hot surfactant paste and stir well.
6. Remove from heat and continue stirring or mashing as the mixture cools to integrate the components.
7. Shape the resulting paste into bars and allow them to harden fully before use.

recipes.name: Rose & Hydrolyzed Silk Facial Solution
recipes.description: A liquid foaming cleanser utilizing Caprylyl/Capryl Glucoside as a primary surfactant and solubilizer. Designed for a pH-balanced, gentle cleanse.
recipes.notes: Caprylyl/Capryl Glucoside acts as both a gentle surfactant and an effective solubilizer for fragrance and essential oils. Substitution with other glucosides may require the addition of a secondary solubilizer like Polysorbate 20.
recipes.process:
1. Measure the surfactant and any essential or fragrance oils into a heat-safe beaker and stir to combine.
2. Add the remaining liquid ingredients one at a time, stirring steadily after each addition.
3. Incorporate the water and hydrosol last, stirring gently to avoid creating excessive foam.
4. Test the pH level and adjust it using a citric or lactic acid solution until it falls between 4.5 and 5.5.
5. Transfer the finished liquid into a foamer bottle.

recipes.name: Sweetgrass & Peg-6 Caprylic/capric Triglycerides Facial Solution
recipes.description: A simplified micellar water featuring sweetgrass hydrosol. Designed for rapid formulation and effective debris removal.
recipes.process:
1. Measure all ingredients directly into a squeeze bottle.
2. Secure the cap and shake the bottle vigorously until the mixture is fully combined.
3. To use, soak a cotton pad with the micellar water and wipe it across the skin until it comes away clean.

recipes.name: Sweetgrass & Iselux Ultra Mild Surfactant Blend Facial Solution
recipes.description: A liquid facial cleanser formulated with mild surfactants, rice protein, and sweetgrass hydrosol. Includes instructions for pH adjustment.
recipes.process:
1. Measure the glycerin, panthenol, surfactant blend, rice protein, and preservative into a heat-safe beaker.
2. Stir to combine, then gently add the distilled water and hydrosol.
3. Test the pH and adjust it to the 5.5–6 range using a citric acid solution.
4. Thicken the cleanser by adding the liquid thickener in small increments, stirring well between each addition.
5. Transfer the finished product to a squeeze bottle.

recipes.name: Coconut & C12–15 Alkyl Benzoate Facial Oil
recipes.description: A fragrant cleansing oil formulated with Cromollient SCE for improved rinse-off. Features a blend of liquid oils for effective cleansing.
recipes.process:
1. Combine all ingredients in a beaker or directly in the final storage bottle.
2. Stir or shake the mixture until it is completely uniform.
3. Transfer to a bottle equipped with a dispensing pump.

recipes.name: Peg-6 Caprylic/capric Triglycerides Facial Gel
recipes.description: A thickened micellar water utilizing a gelling agent for improved handling and application. Provides a gentle, non-stripping cleanse.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the distilled water, micellar surfactant, propanediol, and preservative in a beaker.
2. Stir until the mixture is uniform.
3. Add the gelling agent and continue stirring until the texture is smooth and the liquid is clear.
4. Transfer to a squeeze bottle for storage.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera & Olive Squalane Facial Solution
recipes.description: An amped-up micellar water formulation designed to remove waterproof cosmetics. Features a bi-phase oil-and-water system.
recipes.notes: Biphase formulation incorporating an oil phase for effective removal of waterproof cosmetics. Shake well before each use to ensure uniform application of both phases.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the distilled water, hydrosol, micellar surfactant, and oil in a bottle.
2. Add the preservative and shake until uniform.
3. Note that this formula is bi-phase and should be shaken before each use.

recipes.name: Dried Calendula Petals & Castor Facial Balm
recipes.description: A creamy cleansing balm containing kaolin clay and colloidal oatmeal. Provides gentle physical exfoliation and effective cleansing.
recipes.process:
1. Create a simmering water bath in a small pan.
2. Melt the oil phase ingredients in a heat-safe beaker within the water bath.
3. Prepare an ice bath in a separate bowl.
4. Place the beaker in the ice bath and stir constantly as it cools.
5. Once the mixture reaches a "trace" consistency, stir in the cooling phase ingredients.
6. Pour the final balm into a jar to set.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera & Chamomile Facial Solution
recipes.description: A gentle micellar water formulated with aloe vera juice and hydrosols. Designed for quick, effective cleansing without rinsing.
recipes.process:
1. Measure the distilled water, aloe vera juice, and hydrosol into a bottle.
2. Add the micellar surfactant, glycerin, and preservative.
3. Shake or stir until the mixture is uniform and clear.
4. Store in a bottle with a squeeze or pump top.

recipes.name: Safflower & Shea Facial Solution
recipes.description: An oil-based facial polish containing fine clays and exfoliants. Scented with a blend of fir needle and cardamom essential oils.
recipes.notes: Essential oil blend features fir needle, cardamom, and michelia alba. Refer to standard substitution charts for alternative scent profiles.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the dry ingredients (clays and exfoliants) in a mixing bowl.
2. Stir until the powders are evenly blended.
3. Gradually add the liquid oils and stir until the mixture forms a uniform paste.
4. Package the polish in a wide-mouthed jar.

recipes.name: Champa & Castor Facial Solution
recipes.description: A low-foam, creamy cleansing milk formulated similarly to a lotion. Provides gentle cleansing with a moisturizing finish.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a broad pan.
2. Heat the water phase and oil phase ingredients in separate beakers until melted.
3. Combine the two phases and use an immersion blender to create a stable emulsion.
4. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature, then stir in the preservative and fragrance.
5. Transfer to a pump bottle.

recipes.name: Safflower & Castor Facial Balm
recipes.description: A detoxifying cleansing balm formulated with charcoal and clay. Features sea buckthorn oil and a chocolate-inspired scent.
recipes.notes: Cocoa absolute provides scent but may tint the final product; orange essential oil or fragrance oils are suitable alternatives for maintaining color clarity.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the oil phase ingredients in a heat-safe beaker using a water bath.
2. Stir in the charcoal and clay until no clumps remain and the color is uniform.
3. Place the beaker in an ice bath and stir steadily as it cools.
4. Once the balm thickens to a "trace" consistency, incorporate the cooling phase ingredients.
5. Transfer to a jar and allow it to set completely.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Apricot Kernel Facial Oil
recipes.description: A unique oil-to-gel cleanser utilizing Sucragel as a gelling agent. Transforms into a milk upon contact with water for easy rinsing.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the liquid oils and gelling agent in a heat-safe beaker.
2. Heat the mixture until it becomes clear and the gelling agent is fully dissolved.
3. Stir the mixture occasionally as it cools to room temperature to maintain a uniform gel texture.
4. Transfer the final gel to a squeeze tube.

recipes.name: Coconut & Castor Facial Balm
recipes.description: A squeezable cleansing balm that melts into an oil upon application. Provides a refreshing sensation with eucalyptus and mint essential oils.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the oil phase ingredients in a water bath until fully liquid.
2. Set the container in an ice bath and stir constantly until it reaches a "trace" consistency.
3. Mix in the essential oils until well distributed.
4. Pour the balm into a jar and allow it to set at room temperature.

recipes.name: Hydrolyzed Silk Facial Solution
recipes.description: A concentrated liquid cleanser designed for use in small amounts. Features a blend of mild surfactants and essential oils.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the surfactants, humectants, and active ingredients in a small beaker.
2. Stir gently to avoid creating excessive foam until the mixture is uniform.
3. Incorporate the essential oils and stir well.
4. Transfer the liquid to a dropper bottle for precise dispensing.

recipes.name: Lavender Facial Gel
recipes.description: A wobbly gel cleanser utilizing carrageenan as a gelling agent. Provides a gentle, foaming cleanse with a lavender scent.
recipes.process:
1. Measure the glycerin into a beaker and sprinkle the gelling agent over the surface to prevent clumping.
2. Whisk the mixture and let it sit for at least ten minutes to hydrate.
3. In a separate container, combine the surfactants, hydrosol, water, and preservative.
4. Gradually add the water mixture to the gum mixture, whisking thoroughly after each addition.
5. Verify the pH level is approximately 5.5 and adjust if necessary.
6. Transfer the gel into a jar or bottle.

recipes.name: Rose & Lavender Facial Solution
recipes.description: A gentle micellar water utilizing rose hydrosol and mild surfactants. Designed for effective removal of environmental debris.
recipes.notes: PEG-6 Caprylic/Capric Triglycerides is the primary surfactant, chosen for its non-sticky finish and high compatibility. Substitution is not recommended for maintaining performance.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the distilled water, rose hydrosol, glycerin, and micellar surfactant in a bottle.
2. Add the preservative and shake until the mixture is uniform and clear.
3. Store in a bottle with a squeeze or spray cap.

recipes.name: Safflower & Castor Facial Oil
recipes.description: A viscosity-adjusted cleansing oil featuring eucalyptus and peppermint essential oils. Designed for refreshing morning use.
recipes.notes: Stearic acid can be used at 3% for thickening. Soft butters like mango or shea (10–15%) can be substituted for safflower oil to increase viscosity.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the oil phase ingredients in a water bath until the solid components are completely melted.
2. Remove from heat and allow the mixture to cool, stirring occasionally.
3. Once the liquid is barely warm to the touch, incorporate the vitamin E and essential oils.
4. Transfer the finished cleansing oil into a storage bottle.

recipes.name: Mango & Hydrolyzed Silk Facial Solution
recipes.description: A solid facial cleanser bar formulated with a blend of mild surfactants and butters. Designed for a smooth, non-stripping cleanse.
recipes.notes: Hydrolyzed silk protein (2%) is added for skin conditioning. Substitution with other hydrolyzed proteins is possible.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the primary surfactants in a small saucepan over very low heat.
2. Stir frequently until the mixture forms a smooth, uniform paste.
3. Mix in the secondary heated phase ingredients, stirring until everything is melted and well combined.
4. Pack the resulting paste into a tube or mould and smooth the surface.
5. Allow the cleanser to set for 24 hours before its first use.

recipes.name: White Kaolin Clay & Plum Kernel Facial Cream
recipes.description: An oil-based face mask featuring a blend of stone fruit oils and clays. Designed for deep cleansing and skin softening.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a small saucepan.
2. Measure the oil phase ingredients, clays, and exfoliant into a heat-safe beaker.
3. Heat the mixture in the water bath for 20–30 minutes until fully melted.
4. Stir the mixture with a silicone spatula to ensure it is uniform and free of clumps.
5. Allow the mask to cool before packaging in a jar.

recipes.name: White Kaolin Clay & Safflower Facial Cream
recipes.description: A rich face mask formulated with shea butter, safflower oil, and colloidal oatmeal. Designed for intensive skin hydration and soothing.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the oil phase ingredients in a heat-safe beaker using a water bath.
2. Once melted, stir in the oatmeal and clay until smooth.
3. Continue to stir as the mixture cools to prevent the powders from settling at the bottom.
4. Once the mask has thickened, transfer it into a jar and allow it to set on the counter.

recipes.name: Red Kaolin Clay & Cherry Kernel Facial Mask
recipes.description: A fresh-mixed face mask formulated with cocoa powder, clay, and cherry kernel oil. Designed for immediate use and deep cleansing.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the cocoa powder and oil in a small dish and whisk until smooth.
2. Add the water and whisk again.
3. Gradually sprinkle in the clay while whisking continuously until the mixture is thick, glossy, and creamy.
4. This mask is designed for immediate use and should not be stored long-term.

recipes.name: Safflower & French Green Clay Facial Cream
recipes.description: A clay-based face mask utilizing French green clay and safflower oil. Designed to clarify the skin without excessive drying.
recipes.process:
1. Create a simmering water bath in a small saucepan.
2. Melt the oil phase ingredients in a heat-safe beaker.
3. Stir in the clay and continue to heat for an additional 15 minutes to help break down any clumps.
4. Stir the mixture until uniform and allow it to cool before packaging in a jar.

recipes.name: Fresh Strawberry, Rinsed And Trimmed & Golden Honey Facial Mask
recipes.description: A clay-based face mask formulated with fresh strawberries, honey, and rose hydrosol. Combines the natural acidity of fruit with the absorbent properties of pink and bentonite clays.
recipes.process:
1. Mash the fresh fruit and honey together until the mixture reaches a liquid consistency.
2. Incorporate the hydrosol and mix thoroughly.
3. Gradually add the clays while stirring to achieve a uniform, spreadable paste.
4. Apply to the skin and follow with a moisturizing agent after removal.

recipes.name: Raw Honey & Sweetgrass Facial Mask
recipes.description: A four-ingredient clay mask utilizing sweetgrass hydrosol and raw honey. Formulated with a blend of kaolin and French green clays for a non-drying, deep cleanse.
recipes.notes: Highly customizable basic clay mask. Adjust liquid to clay ratios for preferred application consistency.
recipes.process:

5. Transfer to a squeeze bottle or pump-top container.

recipes.name: 1% Hyaluronic Acid & Argan Facial Lotion

recipes.name: 1% Hyaluronic Acid & Aloe Vera Facial Lotion
recipes.description: A rich, emulsified facial lotion featuring macadamia nut oil and refined shea butter. Scented with frankincense and red mandarin essential oils for a luxurious finish.

recipes.name: Rose & 1% Hyaluronic Acid Facial Lotion
recipes.description: A delicate facial lotion featuring argan oil and rose hydrosol. Includes hydrolyzed silk and calendula extract for a smooth, refined skin feel.

recipes.name: Pomegranate Sterols & Cranberry Facial Cream

2. Remove from heat and stir until the mixture is uniform.
3. Incorporate the cooling phase ingredients and stir well.
4. Pour the mixture into a tin or twist-up tube while still liquid and allow it to solidify at room temperature.

recipes.name: White Sugar & Sweet Almond Facial Scrub 1
recipes.description: An exfoliating lip scrub featuring white sugar suspended in a base of sweet almond oil and stearic acid. Scented with peppermint essential oil for a refreshing finish.

2. Remove from heat and incorporate the sugar and essential oils.
3. Stir steadily as the mixture cools to ensure the sugar remains evenly distributed.
4. Transfer the scrub to small jars and allow it to set completely before use.

recipes.name: Beeswax, Refined & Sweet Almond Oil Balm

4. Pour the liquid balm into tubes or tins and allow it to solidify undisturbed.

recipes.name: Cocoa & Hpa Facial Butter
recipes.description: A decadent lip butter featuring unrefined cocoa butter for a natural chocolate scent. Formulated for high emolliency and protection against environmental dryness.

1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a small saucepan.
2. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a heat-safe container with a pouring spout.
3. Heat in the water bath until all components are fully melted.
4. Remove from heat and stir until uniform.
5. Quickly incorporate the cooling phase ingredients and pour into lip balm tubes or tins.

recipes.name: Polybutene & Blackberry Facial Oil

3. Transfer the oil to a lip gloss or roller-ball tube.

recipes.name: Traditional  Coconut & Sunflower Facial Balm
recipes.description: A classic lip balm formulation featuring beeswax and peppermint essential oil. Designed for a firm, protective consistency and a refreshing cooling effect.

5. Pour the liquid balm into tubes and allow to solidify undisturbed.

recipes.name: Jojoba & Hpa Facial Butter

recipes.name: White Sugar & Sweet Almond Facial Scrub 2

recipes.name: Plum Kernel & Cherry Kernel Facial Balm

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Lanolin Facial Cream

recipes.description: Welcome to the Q&A follow-up post for my Super Simple Natural Lotion formulation! Today I’m tackling some of the questions I got about this formulation that were not answered in the original blog post or video. Can you add goat milk powder?…
recipes.notes: Limit essential oil usage to ≤1% for leave-on safety. Add essential oils to the cooling phase to maintain potency.
recipes.process:
If I want to add essential oils (or fragrance oils), when should I add them?
Could I add powdered goat milk?
Could I use just phenoxyethanol as my preservative? Could I use Geogard Ultra as my preservative instead of Geogard ECT?
Which ingredients impact the pH of a formulation?
Can I add anti-ageing ingredients?
Relevant links & further reading
Similar Formulations
If I want to add essential oils (or fragrance oils), when should I add them?
Add any essential oils to the cool down phase with the preservative, and then carry on with testing and adjusting the pH (if required). Adding a small percentage of essential oils to the formulation will not meaningfully impact the pH of your lotion. Essential oils don't have a pH value as they are not water soluble.
Could I add powdered goat milk?
You can definitely try it! The main concern with incorporating milk of any kind into a formulation is stability as milk is not known for being super shelf-stable, so you'll have to try it and then monitor the formulation for stability.
When starting to formulate with a new ingredient, a great way to get an idea for what can work is looking at sample formulations from suppliers and manufacturers. Lotion Crafter has a goat milk lotion formulation on their website and they note the "formula has passed a USP 51 Preservative Efficacy Test".
The formulation from Lotion Crafter uses 1% goat milk powder in their heated water phase, and that seems like a good place to start. Drop 1% of the distilled water to make room for the milk powder.
You'll notice the Lotion Crafter formulation includes a chelator (Disodium EDTA)—I'd probably incorporate one as well. They use Euxyl® PE 9010 (Phenoxyethanol [and] Ethylhexylglycerin), Potassium Sorbate, and Sodium Benzoate to preserve the formulation, and recommend a final pH of 4.5

3. Remove from heat, incorporate the water, and allow the mixture to cool for one hour.
4. Use an electric mixer to whip the base until light and airy.
5. Stir in the essential oils, mica, and exfoliants before packaging in a jar.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel Body Solution
recipes.description: Detoxifying bath bombs formulated with activated charcoal and Epsom salts. Designed for an effervescent, deep-cleansing bathing experience.
recipes.process:
1. Wear gloves and a dust mask. Combine the liquid ingredients and dye in a small beaker.
2. In a large bowl, whisk the baking soda and Epsom salts until uniform.
3. Gradually incorporate the liquid mixture into the powders, blending thoroughly by hand.
4. Stir in the citric acid and cream of tartar, ensuring the mixture holds its shape when squeezed.
5. Compress the mixture into moulds and allow to dry overnight.

recipes.name: Plantapon Sf Na & Coco Glucoside Body Wash
recipes.description: A self-thickening natural body wash featuring black currant and rose extracts. Formulated with a gentle surfactant blend for a non-stripping cleanse.

ingredients.name: Natural Black Currant, Rose, & Vanilla Fragrance Oil

recipes.process:
1. Combine the surfactants and water-soluble active ingredients in a beaker.
2. Gradually add the distilled water while stirring carefully to minimize bubbles.
3. Cover the container and allow the mixture to sit for five hours to achieve final viscosity.
4. Transfer the liquid body wash to a squeeze tube or pump bottle.

recipes.name: Cranberry Body Solution
recipes.description: Seasonal bath bombs featuring cranberry oil and biodegradable glitter. Designed for high effervescence and a festive skin-softening soak.
recipes.process:
1. Wear gloves and a mask. Blend the liquid carrier oils and dye in a beaker.
2. Whisk the dry base ingredients in a large bowl until smooth.
3. Incorporate the liquids into the powders, blending with gloved hands until the mixture reaches a "wet sand" consistency.
4. Mix in the citric acid and cream of tartar.
5. Press into moulds and allow to dry for 24 hours before decorating with mica and glitter.

recipes.name: Baking Soda & Citric Acid Solution
recipes.description: Multi-layered bath bombs formulated with olive oil and Epsom salts. Designed to provide a luxurious, cake-inspired bathing experience with high effervescence and skin-softening benefits.
recipes.process:
1. Wear gloves and a mask. Combine the liquid carrier oils, solubilizer, and fragrance in a small beaker.
2. Whisk the dry base ingredients in a large bowl. Add any water-soluble dyes to the powder phase.
3. Gradually incorporate the liquid mixture into the powders, blending with gloved hands until the mixture holds its shape when squeezed.
4. Press the mixture into spherical or layered moulds and allow to dry for 24 hours.
5. Decorate with a mica-and-alcohol splatter and biodegradable glitter.

recipes.name: Colloidal Oatmeal & Sweet Almond Body Wash
recipes.description: A solid syndet body wash bar featuring high levels of colloidal oatmeal and a gentle surfactant blend. Formulated to maintain a skin-compatible pH of 5.5 and provide a soft, airy lather.
recipes.notes: Features high levels of colloidal oatmeal for a gentle cleanse. Formulated for reactive skin types.
recipes.process:
1. Wear a dust mask and gloves. Combine the dry surfactants and colloidal oatmeal in a mixing bowl and stir until uniform.
2. Incorporate the liquid carrier oils and humectants into the dry mixture.
3. Knead the mixture thoroughly by hand until it forms a stiff, mouldable dough.
4. If the dough is excessively sticky, add small increments of dry surfactant until the desired consistency is achieved.
5. Press the dough into a mould and allow to air-dry for 3–5 days to harden fully.

recipes.name: Body Solution 1
recipes.description: A premium bath salt formulation featuring a blend of salts and a professional-grade fragrance. Designed for an intensive skin-mineralizing soak and a spa-inspired bathing experience.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the dendritic salt, solubilizer, and fragrance in a beaker.
2. Massage with gloved hands until the liquids are fully absorbed by the salt.
3. Incorporate the Epsom and sea salts, stirring until the mixture is homogeneous.
4. Spread on a tray to air-dry for 48–72 hours before packaging in an airtight container.

recipes.name: Sodium Stearate Body Wash
recipes.description: A high-clarity solid body wash formulated using a heat-process method. Designed for effective cleansing with a smooth skin finish and excellent durability.

ingredients.name: Fragrance Oil Or Essential Oil Of Choice

recipes.process:
1. Preheat an oven to 110°C (~225°F).
2. Heat the primary ingredients in a heat-safe container until they reach a clear, liquid state.
3. Remove from the oven and quickly incorporate the cooling phase ingredients, protecting the balance from heat damage.
4. Pour the mixture into silicone moulds and allow to solidify completely.
5. Unmould the bars once they pull away from the edges and allow to air-dry for 48 hours before use.

recipes.name: Coconut Body Cream
recipes.description: A dense, emulsified shower cream formulated with lavender essential oil. Designed to provide a moisturizing cleanse with a rich, creamy lather and high levels of humectants.

ingredients.name: Lavender Essential Oil Or Fragrance Of Choice

recipes.process:
1. Heat the water phase and oil phase ingredients in separate beakers using a water bath.
2. Combine the phases and blend thoroughly with an immersion blender to form a stable emulsion.
3. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature.
4. Incorporate the cooling phase ingredients and transfer to a storage bottle or pump-top container.

recipes.name: Small Grain Himalayan Pink Salt & Silver-white Biodegradeable Glitter Body Solution
recipes.description: An anhydrous, sparkling bath powder combining the properties of bath salts and bath bombs. Formulated with reflective glitter and high levels of fizzing agents for a shimmering, effervescent soak.
recipes.notes: Silver-white biodegradable glitter (1%) provides shimmer. For an unscented or glitter-free version, substitute glitter with magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt).
recipes.process:
1. Combine the dendritic salt, solubilizer, and fragrance in a mixing bowl and massage until uniform.
2. Incorporate the Epsom salts, sea salt, baking soda, and citric acid.
3. Stir in the decorative glitter and blend with gloved hands.
4. Spread the mixture on a tray to air-dry for 48 hours before packaging in an airtight apothecary jar.

recipes.name: Isopropyl Alcohol & Coconut Body Solution
recipes.description: Seasonal bath bombs featuring high effervescence and a winter-inspired scent. Designed for a slow, luxurious fizz and intensive skin softening.
recipes.process:
1. Wear gloves and a mask. Combine the liquid ingredients in a small beaker.
2. Whisk the dry base ingredients in a large bowl until smooth.
3. Incorporate the liquids into the powders, blending with gloved hands until the mixture holds its shape when squeezed.
4. Press into moulds and allow to dry for 24–48 hours.
5. Optionally, decorate with a mica and alcohol slurry before final drying.

recipes.name: Cocoa  Popping Crystals Body Solution
recipes.description: A unique bath salt formulation featuring cocoa butter popping crystals and full-fat coconut milk powder. Designed for a multi-sensory, skin-softening bathing experience.

ingredients.name: Chocolatey Fragrance Oil Or Cocoa Absolute

recipes.process:
1. Combine the dendritic salt, fragrance, and solubilizer in a mixing bowl.
2. Massage with gloved hands until the liquids are fully absorbed by the salt.
3. Incorporate the Epsom salts, sea salt, coconut milk powder, and popping crystals.
4. Stir gently until uniform and spread on a tray to air-dry for 48 hours.
5. Package in moisture-proof containers.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera & Hydrolyzed Silk Body Wash
recipes.description: A hydrating body wash featuring aloe vera juice and hydrolyzed silk. Formulated with a skin-compatible pH and a mild surfactant blend for gentle cleansing.
recipes.notes: Unscented base has a distinct natural surfactant aroma. Clinical recommendation is to add fragrance, essential oils, or hydrosols to improve olfactory appeal.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the surfactants and water-soluble actives in a beaker.
2. Add the aloe vera juice and distilled water while stirring carefully to minimize foam.
3. Verify the final pH level and adjust to approximately 6 if necessary.
4. Transfer the liquid body wash to a squeeze bottle or pump-top container.

recipes.name: Kaolin Clay & Sodium Laureth Sulfate Body Solution
recipes.description: A mouldable bath dough featuring Sodium Laureth Sulfate for a high-foam experience. Designed for versatility as a character-shaped cleanser or a crumble-in bath additive.

ingredients.name: Bath Safe Essential Oil Or Fragrance Oil Of Choice

recipes.notes: Anhydrous product. Use single-use portions in wet environments to prevent contamination of the bulk batch.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the cornstarch, humectants, and primary surfactant in a mixing bowl.
2. Incorporate the fragrance and preservative, stirring until a dough-like consistency is formed.
3. Divide the dough into sections and knead in micas for varying colors if desired.
4. Store in an airtight container to prevent drying.

recipes.name: Natrasorb & Colloidal Oatmeal Body Solution
recipes.description: A soothing bath salt formulation featuring colloidal oatmeal and Sodium Lauryl Sulfoacetate for a dense, creamy foam. Scented with lavender essential oil for relaxation.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the dendritic salt, colloidal oatmeal, and colorants in a bowl.
2. Incorporate the fragrance, fixatives, and solubilizer, massaging with gloved hands until uniform.
3. Add the Epsom salts and blend thoroughly.
4. Wear a dust mask and stir in the powdered surfactant.
5. Spread on a tray to air-dry for two days before packaging in an airtight jar.

recipes.name: Cocoa Body Solution
recipes.description: Effervescent bath biscuits formulated with unrefined cocoa butter and a fizzing base of baking soda and citric acid. Designed for a moisturizing, chocolate-scented soak.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the cocoa butter and liquid oils in a heat-safe container using a water bath.
2. Combine the dry base ingredients in a large bowl and whisk until smooth.
3. Gradually incorporate the melted oils into the powders, blending with gloved hands.
4. Stir in the decorative beads and popping crystals.
5. Shape the mixture into walnut-sized biscuits and allow to harden overnight.

recipes.name: Body Solution 2
recipes.description: A concentrated liquid bath additive featuring a high load of essential oils and mild surfactants. Designed for use in small quantities to provide aromatherapeutic benefits and a light foam.
recipes.process:
1. Measure all ingredients into a small beaker or directly into the storage bottle.
2. Stir or shake until the mixture is completely uniform and clear.
3. Transfer to a dark glass dropper bottle for precise dispensing.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Shea Body Solution
recipes.description: A rinse-off body conditioner formulated with argan oil and rose hydrosol. Designed to be applied to wet skin during a shower to lock in moisture and provide a silky finish.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the water phase and oil phase ingredients in separate beakers using a water bath.
2. Combine the phases and blend with an immersion blender to form a stable emulsion.
3. Allow the mixture to cool undisturbed until it reaches room temperature.
4. Incorporate the cooling phase ingredients and transfer to a storage jar.

recipes.name: Argan Body Solution
recipes.description: Hydrating bath bombs featuring argan oil and a festive rose scent. Formulated for high effervescence and a skin-softening, petal-pink bath soak.
recipes.process:
1. Wear gloves and a dust mask. Combine the liquid carrier oils and dye in a small dish.
2. Whisk the dry base ingredients in a large bowl until smooth.
3. Incorporate the liquids into the powders, blending with gloved hands until the mixture reaches a "wet sand" consistency.

recipes.name: Isopropyl Alcohol Or Isododecane, As Needed & Apricot Kernel Body Solution
recipes.description: Seasonal bath bombs featuring apricot kernel oil and a cooling conifer scent. Designed for high fizz and a shimmering, purple-tinted bathwater experience.

recipes.name: Isopropyl Alcohol In A Mister, As Needed & Mango Body Mist 1
recipes.description: Vibrant orange bath bombs featuring mango butter and a tropical scent. Formulated with Cream of Tartar for a hard, durable finish and long-lasting effervescence.

recipes.name: Isopropyl Alcohol In A Mister, As Needed & Tucuma Body Mist 1
recipes.description: Festive conifer-scented bath bombs featuring tucuma butter and a seasonal color palette. Formulated for a high stability and an effervescent, skin-softening bath experience.

5. Pack the colors into a spherical mould and press firmly.
6. Allow the bombs to dry for 24 hours before applying decorative mica drizzles.

recipes.name: Isopropyl Alcohol In A Mister, As Needed & Cocoa Body Mist
recipes.description: Festive, tri-colored bath bombs featuring unrefined cocoa butter. Designed with distinct yellow, orange, and white layers for a seasonal skin-softening bath soak.

1. Melt the cocoa butter and carrier oils in a water bath until liquid.
2. Whisk the dry ingredients together in a large bowl.
3. Incorporate the oil phase into the powders and blend until the mixture reaches a "wet sand" consistency.
4. Divide the mixture into three portions and color two of them with orange and yellow micas.
5. Layer the colored portions into a spherical mould and press firmly.
6. Allow to set for 24 hours before use.

recipes.name: Colloidal Oatmeal Body Solution
recipes.description: A concentrated powder bath additive featuring full-fat coconut milk powder and a gentle surfactant. Designed to produce a rich, creamy lather and highly emollient bathwater.
recipes.process:
1. Wear a dust mask and combine all dry ingredients in a mixing bowl.
2. Stir thoroughly, using the back of a spoon to break up any clumps of milk powder.
3. Verify that the surfactants are evenly distributed throughout the powder.
4. Transfer to a moisture-proof jar or bag and store in a dry location.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Meadowfoam Body Oil
recipes.description: A suspension-style body oil featuring colloidal oatmeal and coconut milk powder. Designed to be applied to damp skin to lock in moisture and provide intensive skin soothing.
recipes.process:
1. Process the oatmeal and milk powder in a high-speed grinder until extremely fine.
2. Melt the carrier oils and butters in a water bath.
3. Remove from heat and place in an ice bath, stirring constantly as the mixture cools.
4. Incorporate the powders and vitamin E once the oil reaches room temperature.
5. Transfer to a storage bottle and shake well before application to damp skin.

recipes.name: Body Solution 3
recipes.description: A multi-colored, layered bath additive combining the properties of bath salts and bubble bath. Features a high concentration of surfactants for a dense, latte-like foam.

ingredients.name: Citrus Essential Oil Blend Or Fragrance

recipes.process:
1. Combine the baking soda, citric acid, and powdered surfactant in a large bowl and whisk until smooth.
2. Incorporate the essential oils and blend thoroughly with gloved hands.
3. Divide the powder into three portions and color each with a different citrus-toned mica.
4. Layer the colors into a tall, transparent glass jar to create a parfait effect.
5. Store in a dry location and keep the container tightly sealed.

recipes.name: Body Solution 4
recipes.description: A whimsical, layered bath treatment featuring Himalayan pink salt and high-lather surfactants. Designed for an effervescent, colorful, and highly bubbly bathing experience.

ingredients.name: Essential Oil Blend Or Fragrance Of Choice

recipes.process:
1. Whisk the dry base ingredients and powdered surfactant in a bowl until uniform.
2. Scatter the fragrance oils over the surface and blend with gloved hands until the liquids are absorbed.
3. Divide the mixture into two portions and color with purple and turquoise micas.
4. Layer the colored powders into a glass jar, alternating with a thin layer of Himalayan pink salt.
5. Ensure the container is moisture-proof to prevent premature activation.

recipes.name: Isopropyl Alcohol, As Needed & Isopropyl Alcohol In A Mister, As Needed Body Mist
recipes.description: Victorian-inspired bath bombs featuring shea butter and a lemon-rose scent blend. Formulated for a slow, luxurious fizz and intensive skin emolliency.
